conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be helping take care of you during your stay. Can you tell me your name?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’m Ms. Thompson. I came in because my face was drooping and my right arm felt weak.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You mentioned some facial droop and right-sided weakness. When did this start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It started a few days ago. My sister noticed my face looked off. At first I thought it was just tiredness, but then my arm got weak.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And is the weakness getting better or worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My arm is a little better, but my leg still feels heavy, like I’m dragging it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. You also mentioned some numbness on the right side of your face?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s like a tingling, not sharp pain. And my speech feels a bit slurred sometimes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I noticed that too. We’re going to check for a stroke, but first I need to do a quick exam.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see mild drooping on the right side when you’re at rest, but when you smile, it looks even. That’s interesting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It comes and goes. One nurse said it looked like the left side was drooping earlier.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s important. We’re going to get a CT scan of your head right away to rule out a stroke.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The CT scan is back. Good news — no sign of a stroke, bleeding, or any acute brain issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not a stroke? Then what is it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re not sure yet. Because your symptoms are changing and the scan is normal, we’re going to do an MRI for a closer look.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The MRI results are in. Like the CT, there’s no evidence of a stroke, tumor, or aneurysm.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I really felt weak. It wasn’t in my head.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I believe you. But the neurology team reviewed everything and thinks your symptoms may be related to your liver condition — hepatic encephalopathy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had that before, but I thought I was past it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Encephalopathy can come and go. It can affect your brain function, sometimes causing confusion, speech changes, or even odd neurological symptoms like weakness.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So the face droop and arm weakness could be from my liver?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible. Your exam shows some lingering numbness and mild weakness, but no stroke. We’re going to treat this as encephalopathy for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re increasing your lactulose to four times a day to help clear toxins from your system.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember that from last time. It helps, but it’s not fun.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know. But it’s important to keep your mental clarity and prevent worsening. We’ll monitor how you respond.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I think I’m a little clearer. The numbness is still there, but I don’t feel as foggy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your labs this morning show your liver enzymes were a bit high yesterday, but they’re coming down today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that bad?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s not ideal, but it’s improving. We did an ultrasound of your liver — no ascites, and blood flow is normal. So nothing new there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the blood culture that came back positive?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That showed viridans streptococci, but only in one bottle. It’s likely a skin contaminant, not a real infection. You’ve had no fever, so we’re not treating it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that’s a relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re making progress. Your mental status is better, and your strength seems more stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can think more clearly. But I still feel clumsy with my right hand.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The numbness and mild weakness may take time to resolve. Since your scans are clean, we’ll focus on managing the encephalopathy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news — your liver tests are trending down again. We’re confident this was encephalopathy flare-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, likely tomorrow. We’ll send you home with lactulose four times a day and a follow-up with your primary doctor in three days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I still take my omeprazole? I’ve been on it a while.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We recommend reviewing that with your doctor. PPIs like omeprazole can increase infection risk in cirrhosis if not truly needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my tramadol for pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You can continue it as needed, but avoid opioids and benzodiazepines — they can worsen encephalopathy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve used benzos before for anxiety. Should I stop?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Best to avoid them. Talk to your psychiatrist about safer options. Citalopram and hydroxyzine are okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re clearing you to go home today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. Will the numbness go away?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It should improve over time. Keep taking the lactulose and follow up with labs — CBC, chem-7, LFTs, and coagulation panel.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my transplant status?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re still listed. This episode doesn’t change that. Your MELD score is stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and call if you feel more confused, weak, or unwell.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And I’ll see my doctor in three days for the labs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll fax the results there. You’re cleared to go home with services as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate all the help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Our team is glad you’re feeling better. Stay safe, and we’ll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One last thing — my right eye is still blind, but that’s old, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s chronic and unchanged. No new vision issues. You’re doing well overall.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, Ms. Thompson.
